He is a small-time businessman, seen working operating his various [[Shop]]s. Like other [[Shop]]s and [[Business Scrub]]s, Beedle sells, and sometimes even buys back, quest-specific items, such as [[All-Purpose Bait]] and [[Picolyte]], both of which are not plot-required, but add extra interest to the games. Unlike the other entrepreneurial businesses in ''The Legend of Zelda'' series, Beedle incorporates [[Member's Card|membership]]s into his line of work, rewarding [[Link]] with increased price discounts if he becomes a frequent, repeat customer. ==Biography== ==={{TWW|-}}=== {{Checklist |game= TWW |type= Characters |category= Characters in The Wind Waker |needs= * Detailed information on the character's role in the story, including what quests they are involved in * Detailed information on where the character lives and travels to }} {{Descriptions TWW}} In {{TWW}}, Beedle is a local sea merchant who travels the [[Great Sea]] in search of profit. He is located in [[Beedle's Shop Ship]], a floating shop located near various islands of the Great Sea. There are a total of 11 Beedle Shop Ships on the Great Sea, not including the [[Rock Spire Shop Ship]] which Beedle runs under the guise of an "[[Beedle's Assistant|Assistant Manager]]". Beedle hopes to one day open a chain of trading posts. Bugs, especially beetles, are his favorite thing. Beedle will buy any item in Link's [[Spoils Bag]]. He calls Link "Mr. Customer". Link's first opportunity to meet Beedle is on [[Outset Island]] at the beginning of the game. At this time, Beedle's wares are the [[Bait Bag]], [[All-Purpose Bait]], and [[Hyoi Pear]]s. Beedle later sells [[Bomb]]s, and [[Arrow]]s once Link has obtained the [[Hero's Bow]] and the initial set of Bombs, respectively. Until then, Beedle does not carry Arrows due to circumstances beyond his control, nor Bombs due to [[Bomb-Master Cannon]]'s monopoly on the product. Beedle's wares vary by location. Some locations sell [[Red Potion]], though Link can only buy it once he has a [[Bottle]]. After Link obtains the Bombs from [[Tetra's Ship]], he receives a [[Letter]] from Beedle informing patrons of Bombs becoming available Beedle's Shop Ship. In the Letter, Beedle advertises the shop's "semi-annual Big Chance Extravaganza" and claims to have a special limited-time sale for Bombs. In reality, Beedle sells Bombs at the same price throughout Link's adventure. Enclosed with the Letter is [[Beedle's Chart]], which marks the location of all Beedle Shop Ships including the Rock Spire Shop Ship. When Link purchases his first item, Beedle will make him a [[Member's Card]] so he can collect loyalty points. Link earns one point for each purchase. At 30 points, Beedle grants Link a [[Silver Membership]] and sends him the [[Complimentary ID]] via the [[Island Postal Service]]. Link can give the Complimentary ID to Beedle in exchange for a verbal compliment which refills Link's [[Life Energy]]. At 60 points, Beedle grants Link a [[Gold Membership]] and sends Link a [[Fill-Up Coupon]], which can be redeemed for a full refill of Link's Arrows, Bombs, Life Energy, and [[Magic Meter]]. After Link obtains his first [[Wallet]] upgrade, he receives another Letter advertising the [[Rock Spire Shop Ship]]'s wares: a Bottle, a [[Piece of Heart]], and [[Treasure Chart 4]], which also leads to another Piece of Heart. The Letter is signed "Asst. Manager, Rock Spire Shop Ship". Enclosed is a single [[Green Rupee]]. At the Rock Spire Shop Ship, Beedle wears a face-covering helmet and pretends not to know Link. If Link shows him something from his Spoils Bag, he refuses to buy it and denies being Beedle. ====Letters==== {{Tabs |- | Big Chance Extravaganza | {{Transcript| {{Color TWWHD|Red|Notice from Beedle's Shop Ship!}} It's time for our semi-annual Big Chance Extravaganza! Beedle }} }} ==={{TMC|-}}=== {{Descriptions TMC}} Beedle first appears in [[Hyrule Town]] during the [[Picori Festival]] in {{TMC}}, selling fruits. After [[Princess Zelda]] is turned to stone and [[Link]] obtains the [[Earth Element]] from [[Deepwood Shrine]], he returns to Hyrule Town. In [[Hyrule Town Square]], he can use the [[Gust Jar]] to clear off the dust covering one of the stalls; if Link does this, after he obtains the [[Fire Element]] from the [[Cave of Flames]], Beedle will set up his shop in the stall. Beedle sells [[Picolyte]], and his available selection will expand as Link brings different liquids to the [[Forest Picori]] [[Inside the Barrel House]] of [[Minish Village]]. Beedle's initial selection includes [[Green Picolyte|Green]], [[Red Picolyte|Red]], and [[White Picolyte]], and has three empty bottles to hold more. After Link gives the Forest Picori Inside the Barrel House [[Lon Lon Milk]], [[Mt. Crenel Mineral Water]], and a [[Red Potion]], [[Yellow Pico Bloom|Yellow]], [[Blue Pico Bloom|Blue]], and [[Orange Pico Bloom]]s will grow, and Beedle will begin selling [[Yellow Picolyte|Yellow]], [[Blue Picolyte|Blue]], and [[Orange Picolyte]]. ==={{PH|-}}=== {{Frameless|[[File:Masked Beedle.png|90px|thumb|right|[[Beedle's Assistant]]]]}} In {{PH}}, Beedle operates [[Beedle's Shop Ship]] as in {{TWW|-}}, except that he has only one ship that appears in random locations in the [[World of the Ocean King]]. From 10am to noon on weekends and 10pm to midnight on weekdays (according to the [[Nintendo DS]] clock), the [[Masked Ship]] appears instead, manned by his alter ego [[Beedle's Assistant]]. Beedle sells a [[Bomb Bag]] and a [[Wisdom Gem]]. Beedle's Assistant sells a [[Piece of Heart]] and a [[Courage Gem]]. Both sell [[Potion]]s, [[Ship Part]]s, and [[Treasure]]. Their ships are unaffected by cyclones. The concept of memberships was expanded to include two more levels of membership and member discounts. A [[Member's Card|Silver Membership]] gives a ten percent discount on all items, a [[Member's Card|Gold Membership]] gives a twenty percent discount, [[Member's Card|Platinum Membership]] gives thirty percent and the [[Member's Card|VIP Membership]] forty percent.Discounts or points do not apply to the Masked Beedle's items. Along with Link, [[Tetra]] and [[Salvatore]], as well as [[Tetra's Pirate Crew]] to some extent, Beedle is one of the few characters from {{TWW|-}} to actually reappear in {{PH|-}}. ==={{ST|-}}=== In {{ST}}, Beedle runs [[Beedle's Air Shop]]. Link can see his [[Hot-Air Balloon]] flying around the Overworld prior to actually being able to enter it. At a certain point, Link receives a Letter stating that his Shop just opened. Link can get Beedle's attention from then on by blowing the [[Spirit Train]]'s Train Whistle when he is nearby. He will then land, allowing Link to stop by it like any other [[Station]]. Link can get [[Member's Card|Beedle's Club Membership Cards]], allowing him to save up a point for every ten Rupees spent. After passing certain point milestones, Beedle will grant Link rewards. Saving up 500 points awards Link the [[Heart Container]] sitting at the back of the Shop. ==={{SS|-}}=== {{Descriptions SS}} Beedle appears again in {{SS}}, this time selling wares in a flying house, [[Beedle's Airshop]]. He operates this ship by pedaling a bicycle which powers an electric generator that drives some gears. He sells [[Medal]]s, additional [[Wallet]]s, and his most valuable item, a [[Piece of Heart]]. Asking Beedle about his Piece of Heart before buying it will yield the response that he does not actually know what it is, and picked it up from somewhere nearby and decided to sell it. Should Link look at something of Beedle's and attempt to leave without purchasing anything, Beedle will rant at Link about how much effort he needs to exert to hold Link's weight and decides to punish him by activating a trap door under his feet. During the night, Beedle and his ship retire to an island in the sky called [[Beedle's Island]]. Falling asleep in his ship will allow Link to visit the shopkeeper on his island during the night, and if the young hero falls asleep in his ship during the night, it will return him to [[Skyloft]]. While resting on his island, Beedle will sit and talk with Link whilst admiring the [[Horned Colossus Beetle]] caged in his lap. Here, his diction makes a dramatic change with an above average vocabulary and without the joyful yells he is known for. Link can ask about his altered demeanor, but Beedle does not appear to notice any difference, and will dismiss the question as unimportant. After [[Strich]] settles in the [[Bug Rock]], Beedle will inform Link that his Horned Colossus Beetle has gone missing and asks the young hero to help him look for his prized possession.{{Cite|Ah, I don't suppose you'd be willing to go look for my precious {{Color SS|Blue|Horned Colossus Beetle}}? I'd be grateful if you did!|Beedle|SS}} If Link flies to Bug Rock, he will find out that Strich has discovered a Horned Colossus Beetle. Upon learning that the [[Bug]] belongs to Beedle, he states that he will only let Link have the legendary bug after he plays [[Bug Heaven]], which requires the young hero to catch 10 Bugs in under 3 minutes. If Link succeeds, he will obtain the rare beetle from Strich, and can return the Horned Colossus Beetle to Beedle to receive 5 [[Gratitude Crystals]]. As an additional reward, the shopkeeper allows the hero to buy any item from his Airshop at half price. ==={{BotW|-}}=== {{Stub|BotW}} In {{BotW}}, Beedle can be found walking around Hyrule, mostly close to [[Stable]]s. He travels Hyrule on foot instead of by boat or airship like in previous titles. His backpack is shaped like a [[Bug|Beetle]], which customers can remember him by. Beedle stocks items such as [[Arrow]]s and [[Material#Breath of the Wild|Material]]s, claiming to carry many "special [[Bug]]s." He also offers to buy things from Link, mentioning that gemstones are valuable for earning rupees. If Link speaks to Beedle with a beetle in his inventory, Beedle will ask for it in exchange for a random [[Food]] or [[Elixir]]. His favorite is the [[Energetic Rhino Beetle]], which he says is rare. If Link denies his request, he claims his deal was good and the beetle wants to be with him. He mutters to himself that he'll sneak into Link's inventory and replace it with a regular beetle, but quickly decides to hire someone else to do it. Beedle will excitedly greet anyone who enters his Tent, praising anyone who purchases from him. If all of Beedle's stock is purchased, he will announce that he is going to retrieve new wares. {{Ssb|Shulk}}'s appearance in Beedle's Spirit Battle is a reference to Beedle's attire, whereas [[Toon Link]]'s appearance is an allusion to the [[Hero's Clothes]] worn by Link in {{TWW}} and {{PH}}, as well as the [[Recruit Uniform]] in {{ST}}. The presence of {{Ssb|Gaur Plains}} is likely an allusion to the [[Forest Realm]] of [[New Hyrule]]. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{CoH|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} Beedle is a merchant who hid himself away in order to protect himself from the sudden influx of monsters in [[Hyrule]]. He wants to make a profit off the [[Diamond]]s that monsters drop, selling [[Weapon]]s and other equipment to adventurers in exchange for Diamonds in the hopes of cashing in on them. The location of his shops are random, but there will always be two hidden throughout the land either in the [[Grassland]], [[Cliffs]], or [[Desert]] biomes. His shops are always hidden in caves behind mounds of dirt, which must be dug away by a [[Shovel]] or blown up with an explosive. The goods that he sells are also randomized but he will always sell an [[Bottle]] in each shop for four Diamonds.{{Note|In [[Permadeath Mode]], he sells [[Bottle]]s for the higher price of eight [[Diamond]]s. In Japanese, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, European French, Italian, Latin American Spanish, European Spanish, and Korean, Beedle is named Terry, a diminutive form of Terence.
